title: Rabbi Avin or Ravin bar Sheva
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Chullin 86a mentions him saying, “Since the exiles came up, the meteors ceased,” etc. Hyman considers it very likely that he came from the Land of Israel, bringing the tradition known about Rabbi Chiya and his sons, and descended to Babylonia with the scholars who traveled between the lands. Chullin 48a has Rava saying, “Ravin bar Sheva explained it to me.”

notes.text: Chullin 86a explicitly names Chiya and his sons. Its הזיקין concerns celestial phenomena, not thorns. The claim that the speaker originated in the Land of Israel and later traveled to Babylonia is Hyman’s inference.
The consulted Chullin 86a also offers Ravin bar Abba as an alternative transmitter before Rabbi Avin bar Sheva. That alternative does not establish personal identity or the inferred journey.
